stem: In an X-ray tube, electrons are accelerated through a potential difference of 10^6 volts. What is the minimum wavelength of the X-rays produced?
solution_latex: The minimum wavelength of X-rays produced is given by the equation $\\lambda_{min} = \\frac{hc}{eV}$, where $h$ is Planck's constant, $c$ is the speed of light, $e$ is the elementary charge, and $V$ is the accelerating potential difference. \\\\ Given $h = 6.63 \\times 10^{-34} \\text{ J s}$, $c = 3 \\times 10^8 \\text{ m/s}$, $e = 1.60 \\times 10^{-19} \\text{ C}$, and $V = 10^6 \\text{ V}$. \\\\ $\\lambda_{min} = \\frac{(6.63 \\times 10^{-34} \\text{ J s})(3 \\times 10^8 \\text{ m/s})}{(1.60 \\times 10^{-19} \\text{ C})(10^6 \\text{ V})} = \\frac{1.989 \\times 10^{-25}}{1.60 \times 10^{-13}} \\text{ m} = 1.243125 \\times 10^{-11} \\text{ m} \\approx 1.24 \\times 10^{-11} \\text{ m}$.
